[[File:Kenneth G. Libbrecht.jpg|thumb|Kenneth Libbrecht signs a book.]]
'''Kenneth G. Libbrecht''' <ref>{{Cite web|title=Ken Libbrecht CV|url=http://www.its.caltech.edu/~atomic/cv/kglcv.html|access-date=2021-12-01|website=www.its.caltech.edu}}</ref> is an American physicist whose research has focused on crystal growth, gravitational wave detection, laser cooling and trapping of neutral atoms, helioseismology, and physics laboratory teaching. He has been a Professor of Physics at the [[California Institute of Technology]] (a.k.a. Caltech) since 1984, and he was the physics department chair from 1997-2013.

==Biography==
Libbrecht graduated from [[West Fargo High School]] in 1976, attended one year at the [[University of North Dakota]], and then continued his studies at Caltech, where he received a B.S. in physics in 1980. He further studied as a graduate student under [[Robert Dicke]] at [[Princeton University]], where he measured the solar oblateness as a test of [[General Relativity]], receiving his Ph.D. in 1984.<ref>{{cite thesis |type=PhD |last=Libbrecht |first=K. G. |date=1984 |title=The shape of the Sun |publisher=Princeton University|bibcode=1984PhDT.........3L}}</ref> 

Libbrecht won the 2004 [[National Outdoor Book Award]] (Nature & Environment category) for ''The Snowflake''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2004 Winners of the National Outdoor Book Awards|url=http://www.noba-web.org/books04.htm|access-date=2021-12-01|website=www.noba-web.org}}</ref> Libbrecht was a scientific consultant on snowflakes for the 2013 Film [[Frozen (2013 film)|''Frozen'']].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Olsen|first=Erik|title=The scientist who makes twin snowflakes|url=https://qz.com/1208669/meet-the-scientist-who-makes-identical-snowflakes/|access-date=2021-12-01|website=Quartz|date=16 February 2018 |language=en}}</ref>

Four of Libbrecht's snowflake pictures were selected by the [[United States Postal Service]] as designs for stamps for the 2006 winter holiday season, with a total printing of approximately 3 billion stamps.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Libbrecht|first=Kenneth G.|title=Snowflake Stamps|url=http://www.its.caltech.edu/~atomic/snowcrystals/stamps.htm|access-date=2021-12-01|website=www.its.caltech.edu}}</ref> In 2010, Libbrecht was the recipient of the [[Lennart Nilsson Award]]. In conjunction with the award, the Swedish postal service, [[PostNord Sverige|PostNord]], released a series of stamps featuring some of his images of snowflakes.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Frimärken gnistrar av snökristaller|url=https://www.postnord.com/sv/media/postnord-sverige/2010/frimarken-gnistrar-av-snokristaller|access-date=2021-12-01|website=www.postnord.com|language=sv|archive-date=2021-12-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211201165726/https://www.postnord.com/sv/media/postnord-sverige/2010/frimarken-gnistrar-av-snokristaller|url-status=dead}}</ref>
